Interaction modality: Participants select a sticker whose shape represents the number of people living in their household. The sticker is placed on the map at the location of their home or approximate address.
Values / Encoding: 1 person → half-sphere; 2 people → two touching half-spheres; 3 people → triangle; 4 people → square; 5 people → pentagon; 6 people → hexagon; 7 people → heptagon; 8 people → octagon.

Collected data: Transport mode to the waste-collection point
Interaction modality: Participants indicate the main means of transport they use to reach the waste-collection point. If they use more than one transport mode, they are asked to select the one they use most often.

Collected data: Distance between home and waste-collection point
Interaction modality: Participants measure the distance they usually travel to dispose of waste and cut a piece of string according to the given scale. The string is then attached to the pin marking the waste-collection point on the map.

Participants use a dedicated time ruler, covering the period from 8:00 in the morning to the following day. The ruler is aligned with the map, and participants place a pin at the height corresponding to the time when they usually dispose of waste.
Values / Encoding: Time of day, mapped vertically along the height of the map.

Collected data: Type and frequency of waste disposal
Interaction modality: Participants indicate the type of waste they dispose of through colour coding. They also represent how many times per month they go to the collection point by adding the corresponding number of dots.
Values / Encoding: Pink → PET / plastic bottles / detergent containers / plastic packaging; Blue → glass / glass bottles; Red → residual unsorted waste; Green → organic waste; Yellow → paper and cardboard. Number of dots → number of monthly trips to the Ecopoint.

Interaction modality: Participants add post-it annotations to describe activities, habits, difficulties, or observations connected to their waste-disposal practices.
Participants hang their completed map on the rod corresponding to the neighbourhood where they live.
